questions.q: Which TRL class is used to run RLHF on SQL Pete?
options: SFTTrainer
RewardTrainer
PPOTrainer
DPOTrainer
questions.explain: The lesson uses TRL's PPOTrainer, which implements Proximal Policy Optimization for fine-tuning a policy against a reward function.

questions.q: Why is this training described as RLAIF-style rather than RLHF in the strict sense?
options: Because no reward signal is used at all
Because the reward is produced programmatically by executing SQL, standing in for a human rater
Because it uses a different algorithm than PPO
Because it only trains on AdventureWorks2012
questions.explain: The reward comes from execution correctness, not a human rater, which is why the lesson names it RLAIF-style — automated feedback standing in for human feedback.

questions.q: What checkpoint is the PPOTrainer's policy initialized from?
options: The raw Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct base model, untrained
The sql-pete-sft checkpoint produced by Lesson 16's LoRA fine-tune
A randomly initialized model
Project 2's reward model
questions.explain: RLHF refines an already-reasonable policy rather than starting from scratch, so it initializes from the Lesson 16 SFT checkpoint.

questions.q: In one PPO training step, what is the correct order of operations?
options: Update the policy, then generate completions, then score them
Generate completions from the current policy, score them with the execution-correctness reward, then update the policy
Score random completions, then generate new questions
Train a reward model, then discard it
questions.explain: Each step generates completions, scores them with Lesson 17's reward function, and then calls ppo_trainer.step to update the policy.

questions.q: Why is PPO a good fit for this kind of RLHF/RLAIF training?
options: It guarantees the model will never make a mistake
It bounds how far each update can move the policy, which helps prevent collapse into degenerate outputs that maximize a narrow reward
It removes the need for a reward function entirely
It only works on models smaller than 1 billion parameters
questions.explain: PPO's proximal update constraint keeps training stable, which matters when the reward signal is narrow, like a binary execution-correctness check.
